art_instructions: A wide, low-to-the-ground view shows the owl mid-flight heading from a cozy forest home toward a small schoolhouse. Place Owl (mottled brown-and-cream feathers, large amber eyes, green scarf, tiny cross‑body satchel) in the upper center-right, gliding to the right with wings spread in a soft V and a gentle, happy smile; she should be about one-third of the picture’s height so she is the clear focal point. Add a faint, curved swoosh behind her tracing a left-to-right arc to imply motion. In the left background, include a simple woodland cottage partly peeking from trees (tiny chimney with a small puff of steam and a round window), connected to a curved dirt path that flows across the bottom third of the image. In the right background, show a small, friendly schoolhouse with a triangular roof and a little bell above the door (no text), sized about one-quarter of the picture’s height to read as the destination. Keep the camera low so the path and a few oversized wildflowers and mushrooms are in the close foreground at the bottom edges, making viewers feel short like a child. Use soft early-morning light and a pale pastel sky with two puffy clouds; keep colors gentle with the green scarf as the saturated accent. Maintain clean, sticker-like shapes and minimal shading; never draw any text.
